title: Kettle assurance-claims registry
description: Product-level assurance claims, each naming the evidence it stands on and the changes that stop it applying (#434). The registry points at evidence; it never replaces it. crates/runner/src/assurance.rs is the enforcing parser, and the test suite holds this schema to be no looser.

published.description: The part of the tree that goes public (#478), as repo-relative path prefixes. Evidence outside it is inspectable here and unopenable by a reader of the published site; validation refuses a proven claim that keeps no evidence inside it. Absent means undeclared, which constrains nothing.

id.description: Stable id. Everything joins on it; it must name exactly one claim.

wording.description: The exact or canonical sentence — what a surface quotes.

status.description: The status as recorded. Validation derives the effective status from evidence and never preserves this on trust. failed is a finding, not an error state.

invalidation.description: The changes that stop this claim applying. Mandatory for a proven claim — one that nothing could invalidate is a slogan.

surfaces.description: User-facing places that quote or depend on this claim, as repo-relative paths.

review_route.description: Who or what re-examines this claim — a command to re-run, an issue to reopen.

contradicts.description: Ids of claims this one cannot hold beside. Both halves effectively proven is a refusal.

note.description: Why the status is what it is, when the wording alone cannot say. Prose for the reviewer; validation never reads it.

scope.description: What the claim is about. A declared field constrains the evidence; an undeclared one does not.

model.description: The model file name, as baselines record it.

recorded_against.description: What the baseline evidence was recorded against, beyond what scope names (#489). Recording a value here makes the matching declared invalidation trigger mechanically checkable: validation compares it against the matched baseline report and downgrades the claim when it moves. An absent field is not checked.

bed.description: The bed digest, exactly as the baseline records it (blake3:…).

model.description: The model file name, as baselines record it.

sidecar.description: The sidecar version, as llama-server --version reports it.

expects.description: What the claim asserts the baseline evidence found (#489). Evidence that says the opposite of the sentence cannot go on supporting it; a mismatch downgrades. An absent field is not checked.

verdict.description: The verdict the claim asserts, as the baseline records it.

oneOf.description: An eval baseline written by --write-baseline. Its recorded provenance is compared against the claim's scope and the current scoring version.
An owning test: repo-relative file and test name. Checked to exist; a claim must not stand on a renamed test.
A tracker issue. Context and history, never proof: it can carry a failed or unproven claim but cannot make one proven.
A dynamic or manual release check CI cannot execute. Evidence, with the discipline that it says when it was taken and when it stops counting.
